chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Hammad ibn Bashir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who drinks wine after Allah the Exalted prohibited it upon my tongue, is not deserving of being married to when he proposes, nor to be believed when he narrates, nor interceded for when he intercedes, nor relied upon for an entrustment. So whoever trusts him with an entrustment and he consumes it or wastes it, it is not for the one who entrusted him, upon Allah Mighty and Majestic, that He rewards him or compensates him.'

And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I intended to send goods to Yemen, so I went to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I intend to send so-and-so for the goods.' He said to me, 'Do you not know that he drinks wine?' I said, 'It has reached me from the believers that they say that.' He said to me, 'Believe them, for indeed Allah Mighty and Majestic says: He believes in Allah and believes in the believers.'

Then he said: 'If you send him and the goods perish or are lost, it is not for you upon Allah Mighty and Majestic that He rewards you or compensates you.' So I sent him and he wasted it, and I supplicated to Allah Mighty and Majestic that He reward me. He said: 'O my son, no, it is not for you upon Allah that He rewards you or compensates you.'

I said to him, 'And why is that?' He said to me, 'Indeed Allah Mighty and Majestic says: And do not give away your property to the foolish, which Allah has made for you a means of support. Do you know of any one more foolish than the wine drinker?'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The servant does not cease to be in a leeway from Allah Mighty and Majestic until he drinks wine. So when he drinks it, Allah Mighty and Majestic tears down his protective covering, and his guardian and his brother would be Iblis, may Allah curse him, and his hearing, and his vision, and his hand, and his foot, ushering him to every straying, and turning him away from every goodness.'

key_terms.يُزَوَّجَ: To be married to (in the context of a suitor)

ai.seo_question: What are the legal and spiritual consequences of drinking wine in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the drinker of khamr as 'safiha' (the foolish one), linking the physical act of drinking to a loss of legal credibility (shahada, marriage, trust) and spiritual alienation, where Iblis becomes his guardian. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses the Quranic concept of 'sufaha' to justify trusting reports of drunkenness even if not definitively proven, emphasizing that the drinker's judgment is impaired to the point of spiritual folly. The narrative highlights the transition from being in Allah's 'fusha' (ease) to having one's 'sirbal' (garment of protection) torn away, marking a shift from divine favor to demonic guidance.
